title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X is smooth projective of dimension n (and Y likewise). A_X is the Albanese variety of X and B_X = Pic^0_red(X) is its Picard variety, so that B_X = A_X^* and A_X = B_X^*. A_i denotes i-dimensional cycles, A^i codimension-i cycles, and γ is the ℓ-adic cycle class.

(1) End of the argument begun on the previous page. A 1-cycle given by u: C → X, with C a smooth curve, defines a homomorphism B_X → A_X: pull back to B_C = J_C, identify J_C with A_C by the autoduality of the Jacobian, then push forward to A_X. Cohomologically this map is cup product with γ(C) ∈ H^{2n-2}(X)(n-1). Under the identifications H^1(A_X) ≅ H^1(X) and H^1(B_X) ≅ H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1), it becomes H^1(X) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). This is the Lefschetz operator L^{n-1} in degree 1 when C is a complete-intersection curve.

By the equivalences (i)–(iv) of the previous page, showing that B_X → A_X is an isogeny (a polarization) reduces to the classical fact below. If C is a general complete intersection of very ample divisors, then A_C → A_X is surjective (Lefschetz/Weil for H^1). Hence hard Lefschetz in degree 1 is realized by an isogeny of abelian varieties.

(2) Proposition 2.7. Take a divisorial correspondence D ∈ A^1(X×Y). It gives a homomorphism u_D: A_Y → B_X. Its Künneth (1,1)-component gives a(γ(D)): H^{2n-1}(X,Q_ℓ)(n-1) → H^1(Y,Q_ℓ).
- Claim 1: a(γ(D)) is an isomorphism iff u_D is an isogeny.
- Claim 2: in that case there is Z ∈ A_1(X×Y)⊗Q, independent of ℓ, with a(γ(Z)) = a(γ(D))^{-1}.

Degree check: in X×Y of dimension n+m, a cycle inducing H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X) must have codimension n+m-1, i.e. it is a 1-cycle, as written.

The next page sketches the proof. A commutative square identifies a(γ(D)) with u_D^{(1)} on H^1, via isomorphisms Ψ_X and Φ_Y; this gives Claim 1. Claim 2 then reduces to showing that Ψ_X^{-1} and Φ_Y^{-1} are Q-algebraic. For Ψ_X this is the special case of the Poincaré divisor class on X × B_X, which calls for a canonical 1-cycle on X × B_X.

Purpose: this is part of a programme on the standard conjectures, establishing that the H^1 / H^{2n-1} parts behave 'motivically' through abelian varieties. In effect it proves the Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree 1 and the algebraicity of inverses of isomorphisms between H^1-type cohomologies.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor implicit points: in characteristic p one must use the reduced Picard variety. The 'general' complete-intersection curve must be smooth and connected. The isogeny u_D yields only a quasi-inverse in Hom ⊗ Q, which is why Z lies in A_1(X×Y)⊗Q, as Grothendieck correctly writes.
The proof of Claim 2 is not completed on this page. The Q-algebraicity of Φ_Y^{-1} and Ψ_X^{-1} is only reduced, on the next page, to a special case.

ideas.what: The map B_X → A_X induced by a 1-cycle equals, in cohomology, cup product with its class, H^1(X) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1). For a complete-intersection curve it is an isogeny because A_C → A_X is surjective.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B(X) in degree 1 (hard Lefschetz on H^1 via polarization of the Albanese)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Standard Conjectures, 1968/69) and Kleiman (Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures, 1968); based on Weil's and Lefschetz's theory of Albanese/Picard
ideas.where_published: Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles (Bombay Colloquium 1968, publ. 1969): notes that the conjectures hold for H^1 via abelian varieties; exact wording unsure

ideas.what: Proposition 2.7: a divisorial correspondence D gives an isomorphism H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(Y) iff u_D: A_Y → B_X is an isogeny. The inverse is then induced by an algebraic Q-1-cycle Z, independent of ℓ.
ideas.modern_name: Full faithfulness of h^1 (Picard/Albanese motives) into isogeny classes of abelian varieties; algebraicity of inverses on h^1 and h^{2n-1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck/Kleiman/Lieberman (late 1960s); systematized by Murre (Picard and Albanese motives, 1990) and Scholl (Classical motives, 1994)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Standard Conjectures paper and in Kleiman 1968; not as this exact proposition

ideas.what: Divisorial correspondences D ∈ A^1(X×Y) correspond to homomorphisms A_Y → B_X.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil, Lang (Abelian Varieties); Grothendieck FGA for Picard schemes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard treatment of the degree-1 case of the Lefschetz/standard conjectures through Albanese and Picard varieties. That case was known to Grothendieck and Kleiman and published around 1968–69, and later formalized as Murre's Picard/Albanese motives. Nothing on the page goes beyond the literature.

'en fait en vertu cohomologique' should read 'en fait au point de vue cohomologique'.
'la corr.-prédicats par γ(C)' should read 'le cup-produit par γ(C)'.
The arrow chain is H^1(A_X,Q_ℓ) ≃ H^1(X,Q_ℓ) → H^1(B_X,Q_ℓ) ←~ H^{2n-1}(X,Q_ℓ(n-1)).
'Pour que a(γ(D)) soit un isom, il faut et s. que u_D soit une isogénie' is confirmed.
